seat: a company providing an AI model service: whether the NIS Regulations bind it (as an RDSP or an OES), whether and whom it must notify of an incident, by when (72 hours from awareness), and the most it can be penalised for failing to notify. The Regulations are cyber-security regulations, not an AI law.

scope: Encoded: reg 1(2) definitions deciding scope and 'incident', reg 1(3)(d)-(f), reg 3(1)-(2), reg 8 as a fact, reg 11(1)-(3), reg 12(1), (3), (4), (6)(a), (6)(b) (penalty question only), (7), (9), reg 14A(1)-(2), reg 17(1)(a)-(d) and 17(2)(a)-(d), reg 18(1), (2), (5), (6), (7)(a); EU Regulation 2018/151 Articles 3-4 quoted, inert (Article 4 omitted in the deposited aid text: no threshold there). DEFERRED for time on 2026-10-24: Schedule 2 thresholds, reg 14A(3) time limit. Everything else is a coverage-table row in NOTES.md. Out of scope: UK GDPR breach notification, the AISI template, the Online Safety Act, FCA/PRA reporting, and the Cyber Security and Resilience (NIS) Bill (not law: Lords report stage on 2026-10-24).

forks.F1: Is an AI model API or chat service a 'cloud computing service', 'online search engine' or 'online marketplace'? Asked as three-valued inputs (yes/no/I cannot say), no default; both answers tabulated.
forks.F2: The OES's clock runs from awareness of 'a NIS incident'; the RDSP's from being 'first aware that an incident has occurred'. Each as written; the provider states the moment.
forks.F3: Reg 17(2) does not list reg 12(6) (the RDSP's 72 hours): reading A (late = failure to notify under 12(3)) and reading B (lateness alone not listed) both computed. The independent tester labels the readings the other way round and rates the literal reading (lateness alone not enforceable) the stronger, because 17(1)(c) names all of 11(3) but 17(2)(c) names only 12(5).
forks.F4: 72 hours = 4,320 minutes on one clock the provider names (e.g. UTC); 72h00m in time, 72h01m late; no time zone in the text.
forks.F5: 'Without undue delay': the outer limit only; reg 12(9) has no outer limit (NOTHING).
forks.F6: 'Significant'/'substantial' impact: the provider's determination, asked as a fact; the deposited aid text of EU Regulation 2018/151 gives Article 3's parameters and shows Article 4 omitted, so it sets no numeric threshold (the official text was not checked).
forks.F7: A non-UK provider with no UK representative is not an RDSP on reg 1(3)(e)(i) as written, though reg 14A requires a representative.
forks.F8: 'Information society service' (Directive 2015/1535): asked as a fact.
forks.F9: Enforcement-notice steps taken in time: neither limb of reg 18(7)(a), so not a material contravention; ceiling 1,000,000 pounds.
forks.F10: Reg 18(2) 'regulation (3A)': read as 17(3A); nothing computed depends on it.
forks.F11: Authority's 18(6)(c)/(d) determination not yet made: both ceilings given; the numeric ceiling is the higher.
forks.F12: An OES that is a micro or small enterprise is still an OES; the exclusion is in the RDSP definition only.
forks.F13: Reg 14A(3)(a) 'the coming into force date of these regulations': these Regulations (10 May 2018) or the inserting instrument (S.I. 2019/1444 per Lex; not read); and the three months' counting: not computed.
forks.F14: Reg 12(6)(b) cross-border shortfall: not a 12(5) item and not named in 17(2); a separate 'what happened' option answered on F3's two readings for an RDSP (found by the independent pass).
